You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The `NumericEntityUnescaper.translate` method is responsible for unescaping numeric entities in a given input string. It parses the input to identify numeric entities (e.g., "&#x30") and replaces them with the corresponding Unicode characters.

Looking at the provided code snippet of `NumericEntityUnescaper.translate`, the issue occurs at line 40 where the code checks if there is a numeric entity starting with "&#" within the input string:

```java
if(input.charAt(index) == '&' && index < seqEnd - 1 && input.charAt(index + 1) == '#') {
```

The bug report mentions a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` occurring at index 4, which implies that the index used to access the characters in the input string exceeds the length of the input string.

This condition should be corrected to prevent the index from going out of bounds. The current implementation does not properly handle cases where the input string is too short to contain the expected characters following "&#" which results in the exception.

To fix this issue, the conditional check for the index being less than `seqEnd - 1` should be moved before the `input.charAt(index + 1)` access. This change ensures that the index is within bounds before attempting to access the next character.

Next, I will provide the suggested methods for fixing this issue.

messages.content:
The issue in the `NumericEntityUnescaper.translate` method can be fixed by adjusting the conditional check to ensure the index is within bounds before accessing the characters in the input string.

The correction should be made in the `org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaper.translate` method at the following location:

```java
39 :         if(input.charAt(index) == '&' && index < seqEnd - 1 && input.charAt(index + 1) == '#') {
```

The corrected condition should be:

```java
39 :         if(index < seqEnd - 1 && input.charAt(index) == '&' && input.charAt(index + 1) == '#') {
```

This adjustment ensures that the index is checked against `seqEnd - 1` before attempting to access the characters in the input string.

The suggested location to fix the issue:
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaper.translate(java.lang.CharSequence, int, java.io.Writer)`

This correction will prevent the `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` from occurring when processing input strings containing numeric entities.
